findings.reason: the atomic writer belongs on one named owner (fixed_point.py's publication path, or a shared receipt module it defines) and each other helper belongs beside its existing owner (`canonical_json`/`require_string` at `nova/imas/machine_evidence.py:33,64`), so the plan should split the node or name the single owner it extends rather than collecting five forks under one label.
findings.text: `replan-small-primitives` bundles five independent helpers (uniform-axis validator, read-only array constructor, atomic receipt writer, trimmed-string check, canonical digest) into one work unit, and its "one atomic receipt writer for calibrate/sweep.py, catalog/mast_geometry.py and imas/mast_parity_gate.py" re-implements machinery that already exists at `nova/equilibrium/fixed_point.py:185-215` (temp file, `stream.flush()`, `os.fsync`, `os.replace`, plus a sidecar `.sha256` digest) — a bundle of shallow wrappers over machinery that has already been duplicated at least three times rather than one module that hides the behaviour once

findings.reason: extending `nova/imas/db_entry.py` with the DD-interface/backend policy and routing the 12 direct `imas.DBEntry(...)` construction sites through it is the honest change; a separate opener forks the same ownership and the two will drift, so the finding changes which file the node edits.
findings.text: `replan-dbentry-constructor` proposes "one owned opener [that] carries the DD-version and backend policy" for the 15 call sites, but an owned open already exists as the `DBEntry(imas.DBEntry)` subclass at `nova/imas/db_entry.py:15`, which already takes `uri`, `mode`, `dd_version` and `xml_path`; the plan adds a parallel function without saying why the subclass cannot carry the policy it wants added

findings.reason: the plan must name `nova/database/filepath.py` as the mechanism to extend (or state why it cannot host a data-root resolver) so the census's 177 lines are repaired against the existing owner instead of a second resolver being seeded beside it.
findings.text: `replan-gpfs-data-root` proposes a new "data-root resolver" for the 119 files / 177 lines of hard-coded GPFS paths, but `nova/database/filepath.py:110` (`class FilePath`) is already the path/data-root owner, is built on `nova.definitions.root_dir` and `appdirs`/`fsspec`, and is imported by 9 modules including `nova/database/netcdf.py` and `nova/imas/datasource.py`

findings.reason: one path resolver owned by `nova/database/filepath.py` should serve both the `nova/` product paths and the `benchmarks/`+`scripts/` tooling paths, as the plan itself already commits to `FilePath`-style repo-relative plus absolute-path handling elsewhere; the review changes the plan by collapsing the two nodes' resolver into one named owner.
findings.text: `replan-evidence-tooling-paths` proposes "one resolver with repo-relative receipt paths" for crew run directories and worktree literals in `benchmarks/` and `scripts/`, and `replan-gpfs-data-root` proposes a separate one, so the plan spreads the same path-resolution concern across two nodes and two new resolvers

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — `replan-small-primitives` is a grab-bag of five unrelated single-function helpers rather than one deeper interface, and it silently rebuilds an atomic writer whose owner already exists.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `replan-gpfs-data-root` and `replan-evidence-tooling-paths` each propose a new path resolver without naming the existing owner `nova/database/filepath.py`.
